title: Rabbi Burki or Burkai
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Hyman identifies him as the student of the first Rabbi Mana, as in Jerusalem Talmud Kiddushin, where he raised an objection before Rabbi Mana; in Avodah Zarah 3:6 he taught before Rabbi Mana; and he likewise spoke in Rabbi Yochanan’s name in Yoma 5:6. Rabbi Yitzchak ben Elazar used to call Rabbi Yehoshua son of Rabbi Timi and Rabbi Burki “the holy congregation.” Mavo HaYerushalmi wrote that he was the student of Rabbi Mana, son of Rabbi Yonah, of the fifth generation; Hyman rejects this because Rabbi Yitzchak ben Elazar lived in Rabbi Yochanan’s time.

notes.text: The final ר״י is expanded contextually as Rabbi Yochanan, matching the earlier transmission and Hyman’s chronology argument. The first-versus-later Mana identification and criticism remain attributed.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Yoma 5:6 directly names Burkai transmitting Rabbi Yochanan. This does not independently establish Hyman’s first-versus-later Mana identification or his criticism of Mavo HaYerushalmi.
